solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Duck used in sauces for Far Eastern leaders

indicators.note: the duck is put to use inside the word for sauces
standing in place of, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a supreme (sauce supreme) is a rich cream sauce, here in the plural
the letter furthest to the east, the E at the right-hand end of the word
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A restaurant serving duck in rich sauces to visiting Asian dignitaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far Eastern' is not about Asia: it is the E at the eastern (right-hand) end of SUPREMES, which O replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremos are bosses or people in overall charge, a colloquial synonym for leaders.

clue.text: Ragamuffin taking part in church initiative

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scruffy street child joining in a parish project.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a raggedly dressed, mischievous child of the streets; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Call up energy suppliers on the phone

indicators.note: heard down a telephone line, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: rays carry radiant energy, as the sun's rays do

explanation.surface: Ringing the gas and electricity companies.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone is to contact them by phone or radio, the same as calling them up.

clue.text: Partial to you proceeding with demotion of leader

indicators.note: the first letter is moved further down the word

parts.note: emanating means issuing or proceeding from a source

explanation.surface: Someone who likes you is going along with the boss being downgraded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demotion of leader' moves the opening E of EMANATING three places down. The definition is a joke: a man-eater is literally partial to (fond of eating) you.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating beast has a taste for human flesh, so it is humorously partial to you.

clue.text: Biblical man's upset about two worshippers

indicators.note: the reversed name goes around the other piece
in a down entry, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Seth, third son of Adam, with the possessive S
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man from the Bible is troubled by a couple of devout believers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SETHS into SHTES, which goes 'about' II.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiites are followers of one branch of Islam, so they are a group of worshippers.

clue.text: Popinjays nested around exit

indicators.note: turned around, so the nested letters read backwards

parts.note: popinjays are fops; two FOPs, one nested inside the other, give F-FOP-OP

explanation.surface: Vain dandies huddled around a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Nest FOP inside FOP to get FFOPOP; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop off is slang for to die, a final exit from life.

clue.text: Not great end for top 80s film character The Thing

indicators.note: the end letter of the word that follows

parts.note: ET, the alien from Spielberg's 1982 film
it can mean the thing itself, the very thing

explanation.surface: A film buff's verdict on a sci-fi creature feature: not a great ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit is French for small, the opposite of grand, so it means not great or minor.

clue.text: Amoral man acquired by PM (English) for spin

indicators.note: taken in by, so the rake goes inside the Prime Minister

parts.note: William Pitt, British Prime Minister
a roue is a debauched man

explanation.surface: A scandal-hit English Prime Minister trying to put a spin on a rake's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a full turn on one foot in ballet, a spin.

clue.text: Obligations of chameleon … eat flies

indicators.note: a chameleon changes its colours, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A lizard's duties: eating flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chameleon' signals the rearrangement, playing on the lizard that does eat flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Fealties are pledged duties of loyalty owed by a vassal to a lord.

clue.text: Carry out case

definitions.meaning: to carry out a plan is to put it into practice, as a verb
a lawsuit or legal proceeding brought before a court

explanation.definitionFit: To action something is to carry it out; an action at law is a case.

clue.text: Domestic bird seized by half-cut criminal

indicators.note: held inside the other piece
only half the word survives the cut, here its back half

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A drunken crook grabbing a bird in a household incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' leaves INAL, the second half of criminal, which TERN goes into. 'Half-cut' looks like British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic affairs are internal ones, within a country rather than foreign.

clue.text: Lag behind emergency transport

parts.note: an old lag is a convict, and a lifer is one serving a life sentence
aft is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Falling behind in getting emergency vehicles out.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable raft carried for escaping a sinking ship or aircraft is a means of rescue.

clue.text: Devoted time, in need of practice

parts.note: skills gone rusty need practice

explanation.surface: Someone committed to the cause who has been out of action for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusty servant is loyal and reliable, so devoted.

clue.text: One disputing cowboy shirt retail price, at first

indicators.note: a cowboy job is botched, so these letters are bungled into a new order
only the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone arguing about what a cowboy shirt costs in the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cowboy' looks like it describes the shirt but signals the anagram of SHIRTRETAIL plus P.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairsplitter argues over trivial distinctions, a pedantic person forever disputing details.

clue.text: Longing to eat big cheese on one cracker

indicators.note: the longing swallows the other pieces

parts.note: hunger can mean a strong desire
an MD, managing director, is the boss
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A craving for a large cheese on a cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracker' looks like a biscuit to put cheese on, but it is the definition: informal for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracker, informally, is something excellent, and a humdinger is an outstanding example of its kind.

clue.text: Drinks deliveries with no word of hesitation

indicators.note: the hesitation is left out

parts.note: a deliverance or release is a liberation
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Drinks are delivered without any dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes ER out of LIBERATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Libations are drinks poured as offerings, and jokingly any alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Intruding in vessel, circumventing four on watch, say

indicators.note: going around, so the vase surrounds the numeral

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
watch faces often show four as the Roman numeral IV

explanation.surface: Someone forcing their way aboard a ship, sneaking past the four sailors on watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' and 'watch' suggest a ship and its crew, but here they mean a flower holder and a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Invasive describes something spreading where it is unwelcome, so intruding.

clue.text: Staggering university graduate with two drinks, hugging bachelor

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: the drinks wrap around the other letter

parts.note: gin and ale

explanation.surface: A student staggering after two drinks with a bachelor friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' puts B inside GINALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggering in the sense of astonishing, beyond what one could imagine.

clue.text: Acquisition can be made with this capital, quit stressing

indicators.note: the long word can be formed from this answer's letters together with the other word
under stress the letters are distorted, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip on buying property in a capital city: stop stressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ACQUISITION are those of the answer plus QUIT, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Butcher's frozen flanks — new

indicators.note: the frozen piece's sides lie on either side of the new letter

parts.note: glace means iced or frozen

explanation.surface: A butcher showing off new frozen cuts of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a butcher's is a look, and a glance is a quick look.

clue.text: Scandinavian heading off to join British exile

indicators.note: the trimmed word joins on after the other piece
the first letter is removed

parts.note: Danish, from Denmark

explanation.surface: A Dane setting off to join a British expatriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes D from DANISH, leaving ANISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their country, a verb synonym.

clue.text: House is tall, entirely lacking lift

indicators.note: missing, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: all means completely or entirely

explanation.surface: A tall house with no lift at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes ALL out of tall, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise up, a synonym for lift as a verb.

clue.text: Jeer about principal of horrible comprehensive

indicators.note: around, so the jeer surrounds the letter

parts.note: a catcall is a jeering whistle or shout

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Pupils jeering at the head of a dreadful comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehensive' looks like a school (a British state secondary school), but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all covers everything, so as an adjective it means all-inclusive.

clue.text: What? We mustn't have whiskeys, son can't stand

indicators.note: must go without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet, so two of them are W and W

explanation.surface: An outraged parent: no whiskey for us, the son can't bear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mustn't have' removes both Ws from WHATWE, leaving HATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to be unable to stand it.

clue.text: First answer family doctor within seconds

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
a GP is a family doctor
in means inside

explanation.surface: The family doctor's first response arrives within seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First answer' points to the solution at 1 across, SUPREMOS, which this answer defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosses who matter most, the same kind of top people as the 1 across solution.

clue.text: Trip over centre of huge round container

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: going around, so the middle letters surround the container
the middle letters of the word that follows

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Tripping over the middle of a huge round container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of 'Trip over', but it gives O, the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short excursion or jaunt, a trip.

clue.text: Picked up net stocking left behind in flat

indicators.note: keeping in stock, so the outer letters hold the other piece
the rear letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to net money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Collecting a net stocking someone left behind in the apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like the garment but signals EARN held inside L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Picked up as in acquired a skill or knowledge, which is what learnt means.

clue.text: Uncovered vast issue about ship to be reviewed

indicators.note: with its outer letters taken off
around, so the offspring surrounds the ship

parts.note: seed means offspring or issue
SS, steamship

explanation.surface: A huge problem about a vessel has been exposed and must be reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' here means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assessed is to be evaluated or appraised, so reviewed.
